closes.text: BUILT (BREAKING by rule; import-foundation.md §9 slice 1). A selector subject may start at a ROOT (`pkg`/`std`/a dependency) anywhere in the type - tuple elements, generic arguments, array elements, closure types: `(impl pkg::lib::overlay::Overlay)`, `(impl (pkg::d::T, std::e::U))`. Resolution happens in the type drain and only when the head binds nothing in the file's scope, so the bare-name and module-qualified rules are unchanged (the kolt copy's `(impl Overlay)` and `(impl bool with Display)` still admit); root-headed paths descend through directory children as import paths do. The bare one-selector form `m::(impl T)` / `m::(impl T)::first` parses; fmt collapses a one-selector set to it (braces only with two or more members); the token net agrees; a selector at an import's HEAD (no module before it) is refused (`import #(impl T);` used to parse silently). `(impl *)` is the whole-module selector; `(impl _)` is read as `(impl *)` with an error this release and refused next (the paper's Q6), and fmt rewrites it; `as self` / `as super` are refused (Q3; estate 0). Four ledger rows NEW (the `*` steer, the reserved alias, and two for A182's glob), rows 491/496 re-keyed `_`->`*`. The 24 in-repo `(impl _)` lines moved (13 in module_resolution.rs). On the way: a qualified impl head (`impl m::Box<type T>`) now registers its binders. Estate: std/corpus/docs/website 0; KOLT 21 `(impl _)` lines in 18 files (20 errors on each entry; the owner's patch lang-56b/kolt-a181-impl-star.patch - with it both entries check clean) + 4 lone-selector sets fmt will collapse (drift only). Spec names.md, grammar.md updated; CHANGELOG `breaking`.

FIXED. B688's quick fix for a block in a USER module now emits the admission itself - `import {module}::(impl {absolute subject});` (e.g. `import pkg::styles::(impl std::web::style::Style);`) - instead of the module's first export; the sentence still names the block. Std blocks keep std's steer-index trait import. Pinned on the B688 repro (the fix text); the B688 user-module fix text in the pins updated.

BUILT (BREAKING; import-foundation.md §8 leaf-only admission). One rule - 'what a statement carries' - now drives B688's reach, B401's lookup admission and B318's post-build admission: the LEAF module (for a selector, the module it stands under) plus an item leaf's own file; parent directory bodies are no longer carried (names.md §4.1's directory-body paragraph retired). A re-exported selector admission (`export import a::(impl T);`) travels to importers and, via a package prelude, to every file of the package (Q8); `export import m::*;` (the glob re-export) is NEW - a plain glob import is refused, and so is a glob over a non-module (two ledger rows). Retired on the way: `statement_sources`, `ancestor_module_sources`, the path index, the analyzer's `source_paths`. Deviation to note: re-exported admissions work per FILE as B688's reach does (a re-exported `(impl T)` admits the block's FILE in importers); only `export import`s that write a selector travel, plain re-exports do not (B515 intact). The compiler-run census: std, corpus, docs 0 files lose a method; website copy `vilan check` clean 0; kolt copy 0 files lose a method (its only errors are A181's `(impl _)` steer). The P7 B318 pins now refused (renamed `…_no_longer_admitted_by_a_childs_import`, `only_declines_the_impls_its_leaf_carries`); plant-proven (the path-rule plant, the re-exported-admission pins). Docs appendix/editor.md; CHANGELOG `breaking`.
